components.note: 氵 (water) — soup is a hot liquid
昜 (yáng) gives a loose sound hint — shared -ang ending, different initial

example.pinyin: Zhè wǎn tāng hěn hǎohē.
example.english: This bowl of soup is very tasty.
example.fact: In Chinese meals, 汤 is often drunk alongside the food rather than served as a starter. 汤圆 are sweet glutinous rice balls in a soup, traditionally eaten at the Lantern Festival. The classical sense 'hot water' survives in the idiom 赴汤蹈火, 'go through fire and water'.

components.note: The traditional 麗 had a deer (鹿) below paired antler-like shapes; the simplified form keeps only the paired shapes, and 'pair' is the root of the idea of elegance.

example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng hěn měilì.
example.english: The scenery here is beautiful.
example.fact: 丽 almost always appears in compounds: 美丽 (beautiful), 华丽 (gorgeous), 秀丽 (graceful). It is a very common element in given names, such as 丽丽 and 美丽. The simplified 丽 is not related in shape to 鹿 any more, though the traditional form is.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — a container
合 (hé) gives the sound — identical in pinyin, and it means 'to close together', like a lid fitting

example.pinyin: Zhège hézi lǐ yǒu shénme?
example.english: What's in this box?
example.fact: 盒 is a small box with a lid, as in 饭盒 (lunch box), 文具盒 (pencil case) and 盒饭 (boxed meal). It doubles as a measure word, 一盒巧克力 (a box of chocolates). A large box is 箱 (xiāng).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — an interjection you voice aloud
艾 (ài) gives the sound — same syllable, different tone

example.pinyin: Āi, nǐ de shǒujī zài zhèr!
example.english: Hey, your phone is right here!
example.fact: 哎 is used to get someone's attention or to express mild surprise or regret. 哎呀 is a stronger 'oh no/oh my', and 哎哟 reacts to pain or surprise. Tones can vary with the mood, so pitch carries emotion here.

components.note: 氵 (water) — swimming happens in water
斿 (yóu) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zài hǎi lǐ yóuyǒng.
example.english: I like swimming in the sea.
example.fact: 游 covers both 'swim' and 'roam': 游泳 (to swim), 旅游 (to travel), 游客 (tourist), 游戏 (game). The idea in both senses is moving freely, floating or wandering without a fixed route.

components.note: 女 (woman) — early surnames are often linked to maternal clans
生 (shēng) gives a loose sound hint — shared -eng/-ing ending; it also means 'to be born'

example.pinyin: Nǐ xìng shénme?
example.english: What is your surname?
example.fact: 姓 is both a noun (surname) and a verb ('to be surnamed'): 我姓李. The polite way to ask is 您贵姓? Chinese surnames come first and given names second. 老百姓 literally 'old hundred surnames' means ordinary people.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a visitor who comes under your roof
各 (gè) — a person arriving, also a loose sound hint for kè

example.pinyin: Jīntiān wǎnshang yǒu kèrén lái.
example.english: We have guests coming tonight.
example.fact: 客 is central to Chinese hospitality: 客人 (guest), 客气 (polite), and 不客气 ('you're welcome'). 客厅 is the living room, literally the 'guest hall'. 做客 means to be a guest at someone's home.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread) — the word first graded the quality of silk thread
及 (jí) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.pinyin: Nǐ zài jǐ niánjí?
example.english: What grade are you in?
example.fact: 级 names levels and ranks: 年级 (school year), 高级 (advanced), 初级 (beginner), 升级 (to upgrade). It is also the measure word for steps and levels, as in language exams and rankings like HSK.

components.note: A food vessel with a lid on top, picturing a meal being served.

example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de shíwù hěn hǎochī.
example.english: The food here is very delicious.
example.fact: In everyday speech 'to eat' is 吃, while 食 is the formal and bound form: 食物 (food), 食堂 (canteen), 素食 (vegetarian food). The saying 民以食为天 means food is heaven to the people.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — fastening is done by hand
口 (kǒu) gives the sound — same syllable, different tone

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ kòuzi kòu hǎo.
example.english: Please button up properly.
example.fact: 扣 is the verb 'to fasten', and 扣子 is the button. It also means 'to deduct': 扣钱 (deduct pay), 扣分 (deduct points). In shops, 折扣 is a discount, but 打八折 means 20% off because 八折 is 80% of the price.

components.note: 才 (cái) gives a loose sound hint — similar start and ending
子 (child, seed) — something kept and preserved, as a seed is saved for later

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bǎ qián cún zài yínháng lǐ.
example.english: I want to deposit money in the bank.
example.fact: 存 covers keeping, saving and existing: 存钱 (deposit money), 存款 (savings), 保存 (to save a file), 存在 (to exist), 存包 (check a bag). Computer users say 存 for saving a document.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — the smell of ripening grain
日 — the lower part, from an old 甘 (sweet) shape in this character

example.pinyin: Zhè duǒ huā hěn xiāng.
example.english: This flower smells lovely.
example.fact: 香 means good-smelling and also appetizing: 好香 is said of both flowers and food. It builds 香水 (perfume), 香蕉 (banana) and 香港 (Hong Kong, 'fragrant harbor'). 烧香 (burning incense) is a temple custom.

components.note: 一 (one) — the numeral part
白 (bái) gives the sound — same syllable, different tone

example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū yǒu sānbǎi yè.
example.english: This book has three hundred pages.
example.fact: 百 also means 'all, many': 百货 (department store goods), 百姓 (common people), 百科 (encyclopedic). Percentages use 百分之: 百分之五十 is fifty percent. Note 一百 is yìbǎi with a changed tone for 一.

components.note: 日 (sun) — the old sense is the halo around the sun
军 (jūn) gives a loose sound hint — shared vowel, different ending

example.pinyin: Wǒ tóu yǒudiǎn yūn.
example.english: I feel a little dizzy.
example.fact: 晕 is 'dizzy' as in 头晕, and 晕倒 means to faint. Motion sickness words, 晕车 (carsick) and 晕船 (seasick), are normally read yùn, the same reading used in 光晕 (halo).

components.note: Often traced to a jade pendant; the color meaning is a borrowing and the picture does not literally show yellow.

example.pinyin: Qiūtiān shùyè dōu biàn huáng le.
example.english: In autumn the leaves all turn yellow.
example.fact: Yellow was the imperial color of China. 黄河 is the Yellow River, and Chinese people are often called 'descendants of the Yellow Emperor'. 黄 has slang meanings too: 黄色 can mean pornographic, and 黄了 means a plan fell through.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — the old sense is 'sharp' or 'severe'
居 (jū) gives the sound — close, differing in tone

example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan kàn diànshìjù.
example.english: I like watching TV series.
example.fact: 剧 means drama in 电视剧 (TV series), 京剧 (Peking opera), 话剧 (stage play) and 剧院 (theater). 追剧, 'to chase a series', is the everyday term for binge-watching. It can also mean intense: 剧烈.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — snow falls from the sky like rain
彐 — traditionally the sound part, though its link to xuě is hard to see today

example.pinyin: Běijīng dōngtiān chángcháng xià xuě.
example.english: It often snows in Beijing in winter.
example.fact: 'To snow' is 下雪, using 下 'to fall', just like 下雨. 小雪 and 大雪 are two of the 24 solar terms. The classical meaning 'to wipe away' lives on in 雪耻, to wipe away shame.

components.note: 贝 (shell) — the old money radical, so valuables and prices

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu tài guì le.
example.english: This piece of clothing is too expensive.
example.fact: 贵 means costly, and also honored: 贵姓 asks 'your honorable surname', and 贵国 means 'your country'. It is also the abbreviation for Guizhou province (贵州). It is the opposite of 便宜 for price.

components.note: 车 (cart) — carrying goods on a vehicle
哉 (zāi) gives the sound — close, differing in the tone

example.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē kěyǐ zài wǔ gè rén.
example.english: This car can carry five people.
example.fact: 载 is read zài for 'carry' (装载, 载客) and in 下载 (to download). Read zǎi, it means 'to record' or 'year': 记载 (to record), 转载 (to repost), 三年五载 (several years).

components.note: 辶 (walk) — chasing and catching up
隶 (lì) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Māo dǎizhù le yì zhī lǎoshǔ.
example.english: The cat caught a mouse.
example.fact: 逮 is read dǎi in the colloquial sense 'to catch' (逮鱼, 逮蚊子). In the formal word 逮捕 (to arrest) it is read dài. The colloquial reading is common in northern Mandarin.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — early mirrors were polished bronze
竟 (jìng) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.pinyin: Tā zài zhào jìngzi.
example.english: She is looking in the mirror.
example.fact: 镜 builds many useful words: 镜子 (mirror), 眼镜 (glasses), 镜头 (camera lens), 望远镜 (telescope). A classical saying, 以史为镜, urges you to use history as a mirror.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — body fat
巴 (bā) gives a loose sound hint — shared -a/-ei is not close

example.pinyin: Zhè zhī māo tài féi le.
example.english: This cat is too fat.
example.fact: 肥 describes animals and meat (肥肉, fatty meat). For people, 胖 (pàng) is less harsh, and calling someone 肥 is rude. 肥 is also fertile or loose-fitting (肥沃, 肥大), and 减肥 is to go on a diet; 肥料 means fertilizer.

components.note: 片 (slab) — a wooden board used for printing
反 (fǎn) gives a loose sound hint — shared -an ending

example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū yǒu xīnbǎn.
example.english: This book has a new edition.
example.fact: 版 started as a printing block. It now covers editions and versions: 第二版 (second edition), 出版 (to publish), 版权 (copyright), 盗版 (pirated edition), 网页版 (web version).

components.note: A bent, winding shape, often read as a curved container or basket, the root of the idea 'bent' and, by extension, a winding melody.

example.pinyin: Zhè shǒu qǔzi hěn hǎotīng.
example.english: This tune sounds lovely.
example.fact: 曲 is read qǔ for songs and music: 歌曲 (song), 作曲 (compose), 曲调 (melody). Read qū, it means bent: 弯曲 (to curve), 曲线 (curve), 曲折 (winding). Yuan-dynasty 曲 is a famous verse form.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — needles are made of metal
十 — a straight line crossed like a pin or thread, picturing the needle

example.pinyin: Hùshi gěi wǒ dǎ le yì zhēn.
example.english: The nurse gave me an injection.
example.fact: 针 is a needle, and 打针 is to get an injection. It forms 针灸 (acupuncture) and 指南针 (compass), literally 'south-pointing needle'. 针 also counts shots and stitches.

components.note: 土 (earth) — the old sense is filling a hole with earth
真 (zhēn) gives a loose sound hint — shared -n ending, different initial

example.pinyin: Qǐng tián yíxià zhè zhāng biǎo.
example.english: Please fill in this form.
example.fact: 填 is the verb for filling blanks on forms: 填表 (fill out a form), 填空 (fill in the blank), 填写 (complete). It also means filling a hole or gap, and 填饱肚子 means to fill your stomach.

components.note: 门 (door) — a doorway
人 (person) — someone glimpsed for a moment in a doorway

example.pinyin: Tiānkōng zhōng shǎn guò yí dào guāng.
example.english: A beam of light flashed across the sky.
example.fact: 闪 gives 闪电 (lightning), 闪光灯 (camera flash) and 闪开 ('get out of the way'). Colloquially 闪了腰 means to throw out your back, and 闪婚 is a 'flash marriage' to someone you've known only briefly.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — iron is a metal
失 (shī) stands in for the sound part of 鐵 in simplification — only a loose match

example.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zuò dìtiě shàngbān.
example.english: I take the subway to work every day.
example.fact: 铁 forms transport words: 铁路 (railway), 地铁 (subway), 高铁 (high-speed rail). It also means 'firm, ironclad': 铁了心 is to be totally determined, and 铁哥们 means a very close male friend.

components.note: 皀 (food vessel) — a meal being eaten
旡 (a person turning away) — someone who has finished eating, hence 'already'

example.hanzi: 既然你来了,就一起吃饭吧。
example.pinyin: Jìrán nǐ lái le, jiù yìqǐ chīfàn ba.
example.english: Since you're here, let's eat together.
example.fact: 既 gives two useful patterns: 既然…就… ('since… then…') and 既…又… ('both… and…'), as in 既便宜又好吃 (both cheap and tasty). Its sibling 即 shows a person facing the food instead.

components.note: 攴 (tap, strike) — a hitting action
高 (gāo) gives a loose sound hint — shared -ao ending

example.pinyin: Qǐng xiān qiāo mén.
example.english: Please knock on the door first.
example.fact: 敲 is the standard verb for knocking: 敲门 (knock on a door), 敲键盘 (tap a keyboard). 敲定 means to settle or finalize, and 敲竹杠 is slang for overcharging.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — winding thread around something
尧 (yáo) gives a loose sound hint — shared -ao ending

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù yào rào hěn yuǎn.
example.english: You have to go a long way around on this road.
example.fact: 绕 means to circle, wind or take a detour: 绕路 (detour), 围绕 (revolve around), 绕口令 (tongue twister). 绕圈子 literally 'go in circles' means to beat around the bush.

components.note: 页 (head) — the neck is just below the head
令 (lìng) gives the sound — close, differing in tone

example.pinyin: Lǎoshī lǐng háizimen guò mǎlù.
example.english: The teacher leads the children across the road.
example.fact: 领 began as 'neck' and extended to collar (衣领, 领带 for necktie), to lead (带领, 领导) and to receive (领奖, 领钱). Leading people is like grabbing them by the collar.

components.note: 氵 (water) — smooth, slippery flow
留 (liú) gives the sound — close, differing in tone

example.pinyin: Tā tōutōu liū chūqù le.
example.english: He sneaked out.
example.fact: 溜 is about moving smoothly or stealthily: 溜走 (slip away), 溜冰 (ice skate), 溜达 (to stroll). 滑溜 describes something slippery or smooth.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — it is a plant
乂 (yì) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Duānwǔ Jié rénmen huì guà àicǎo.
example.english: People hang mugwort during the Dragon Boat Festival.
example.fact: 艾 is mugwort, burned in moxibustion (艾灸) and hung on doors at the Dragon Boat Festival to ward off evil. It is also a surname and used in transliterations such as 艾滋病 (AIDS).

components.note: 取 — the top part, which also shows the idea of collecting
乑 (three people) — a crowd gathering

example.hanzi: 周末朋友们聚在一起吃饭。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò péngyoumen jù zài yìqǐ chīfàn.
example.english: On the weekend, friends gather for a meal.
example.fact: 聚 is for people or things coming together: 聚会 (get-together), 聚餐 (group meal), 团聚 (reunion), 聚焦 (to focus). Its opposite is 散 (sàn), and 聚散 means meeting and parting.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — the old meaning is dividing up and setting in order
歹 — the left part, a bone fragment, with no clear modern link

example.hanzi: 请把名字列在这张表上。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ míngzi liè zài zhè zhāng biǎo shàng.
example.english: Please list the names on this table.
example.fact: 列 means to line up or list: 列表 (list), 列出 (list out), 排列 (to arrange). It is also the measure word for trains: 一列火车. 列车 is a formal word for a train.

components.note: 氵 (water) — wetness
显 (xiǎn) comes from the sound part of the traditional form — a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Wǒ de yīfu shī le.
example.english: My clothes are wet.
example.fact: 湿 gives 潮湿 (humid), 湿度 (humidity), 湿巾 (wet wipe) and 湿透 (soaked). In traditional Chinese medicine, 湿气 ('dampness') is a common idea in wellness advice.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — holding or propping up
掌 (zhǎng) gives a loose sound hint — shared -ang/-eng ending

example.pinyin: Tā yòng shǒu chēng zhe tóu.
example.english: He rests his head on his hand.
example.fact: 撑 means to hold up or push with a pole: 撑伞 (hold up an umbrella), 支撑 (support), 撑船 (pole a boat). Colloquially 吃撑了 or 撑死了 means 'stuffed from eating too much'.

components.note: A drawing of a snake-like creature; as a radical it marks insects and reptiles.

example.pinyin: Shù shàng yǒu hěn duō chóngzi.
example.english: There are many bugs in the tree.
example.fact: 虫 is the simplified form of 蟲, which stacked three 虫 for 'many crawling creatures'. It is the radical in 蛇, 蚂蚁 and 蝴蝶. Add 子 for 虫子 (bug), 昆虫 (insect) and 害虫 (pest).

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person given a role
壬 (rén) gives the sound — close, differing in tone

example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen de bānzhǔrèn.
example.english: He is our class teacher.
example.fact: 任 builds 责任 (responsibility), 任务 (task), 任何 (any), 信任 (trust) and 任性 (willful). As a surname it is read Rén.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — dividing materials into measured portions
齐 (qí) gives a loose sound hint — shared -i ending

example.pinyin: Yīshēng gěi wǒ kāi le yí jì yào.
example.english: The doctor prescribed me a dose of medicine.
example.fact: 剂 is a measure word for doses of herbal medicine (一剂中药) and appears in 药剂 (pharmaceutical), 试剂 (reagent) and 针剂 (injection). 强心剂 is literally a 'heart tonic', used figuratively for a morale boost.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a companion
火 (huǒ) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de hǎo huǒbàn.
example.english: He is my good partner.
example.fact: 伙 builds 伙伴 (partner), 同伙 (accomplice) and 伙食 (meals served in a group kitchen). It is also a measure word for groups of people: 一伙人, often with a faintly negative tone, like 'a gang'.

components.note: 苟 (gǒu) — the left part; its link to 'respect' is debated
攴 (tap, strike) — an action radical

example.pinyin: Wǒmen dōu hěn zūnjìng lǎoshī.
example.english: We all respect our teacher.
example.fact: 敬 means to respect and also to offer politely: 敬酒 is to toast someone at a banquet and show respect. 敬礼 is a salute, 恭敬 is respectful, and 敬酒不吃吃罚酒 is the idiom for refusing a polite offer.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — holding something up to block
当 (dāng) gives the sound — close, differing in tone

example.pinyin: Bié dǎngzhù wǒ de lù.
example.english: Don't block my way.
example.fact: 挡 is to block or shield: 挡住 (block), 阻挡 (obstruct), 挡风 (shelter from wind). On a car, 挡 is also a gear: 换挡 (shift gears), 一挡 (first gear).

components.note: 禾 (grain) — rice seedlings transplanted from one place to another
多 (duō) gives a loose sound hint — a distant match

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhuōzi wǎng zuǒ yí yìdiǎn.
example.english: Please move the table a little to the left.
example.fact: 移 means to shift something, and is the root of 移动 (to move; also 'mobile'), 移民 (to immigrate) and 转移 (to transfer). The tale 愚公移山 tells of a man who tried to move mountains with perseverance.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — pushing and flicking by hand
发 (fā) gives a loose sound hint — the same vowel but different initial

example.pinyin: Qǐng bō zhège diànhuà hàomǎ.
example.english: Please dial this phone number.
example.fact: 拨 means to push aside or flick, and so to dial: 拨号 (dial), 拨打电话 (make a call). It also means to allocate (拨款, release funds), and counts batches of people as 一拨人.

components.note: 皀 (food vessel) — a meal ready to eat
卩 (kneeling person) — a person sitting down to eat, hence approaching or immediacy

example.hanzi: 他一听到消息,即刻出发了。
example.pinyin: Tā yì tīngdào xiāoxi, jíkè chūfā le.
example.english: As soon as he heard the news, he set off at once.
example.fact: 即 is formal 'immediately/namely': 即将 (about to), 即使 (even if), 立即 (immediately). It is a counterpart to 既, which shows the same person turning away from the food.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — a country's borders
玉 (jade) — a treasure kept inside the borders

example.pinyin: Nǐ shì nǎ guó rén?
example.english: What country are you from?
example.fact: 国 appears in the names of countries: 中国, 美国 (literally 'beautiful country'), 英国, 法国. 中国 originally meant 'central state'. 国家 means country or nation, and 外国 means foreign country.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — drawing a bow
丨 — a stroke standing for the bowstring pulled back

example.hanzi: 这个故事吸引了很多人。
example.pinyin: Zhège gùshi xīyǐn le hěn duō rén.
example.english: This story attracted many people.
example.fact: 引 started as drawing a bow and extends to attracting and quoting: 吸引 (attract), 引起 (cause), 引用 (quote), 引导 (guide). 引号 are quotation marks, and 引擎 is a transliteration of 'engine'.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a pine is a tree
公 (gōng) gives a loose sound hint — shared -ong ending

example.pinyin: Nǐ de xiédài sōng le.
example.english: Your shoelace has come loose.
example.fact: 松 is both 'pine' and 'loose': the 'loose' meaning was once written with a different character, 鬆, and merged into 松 when simplified. It builds 放松 and 轻松 (to relax). The pine is a symbol of endurance in 岁寒三友, the three friends of winter.
